title: Platform for high repetition rate proton stopping power measurements in Warm Dense Matter
abstract:
<jats:title>Abstract</jats:title>
                  <jats:p>We present a high-repetition-rate experimental platform for proton stopping-power measurements in warm dense matter in a regime where the projectile velocity approaches the electron thermal velocity and theoretical predictions remain highly uncertain. The platform combines laser-driven proton generation via target normal sheath acceleration with a compact magnetic energy selector to produce quasi-monoenergetic proton beams in the 0.3–0.6 MeV range with energy bandwidths of tens of keV and sub-nanosecond duration. Warm dense matter is generated by femtosecond laser heating of thin carbon foils and characterized using streaked optical pyrometry and x-ray pinhole grating spectroscopy, supported by radiation-hydrodynamic simulations. We further investigate the present limitations of the approach, including uncertainties in sample conditions, finite proton bunch duration, and proton scattering, and discuss pathways toward improved measurements. The results demonstrate a versatile and scalable approach for systematic, high-statistics studies of ion stopping power in warm dense matter relevant to inertial confinement fusion and charged-particle transport in high-energy-density plasmas.</jats:p>

title: K-epsilon modelling of turbulent transport in the edge-SOL boundary layer
abstract:
<jats:title>Abstract</jats:title>
                  <jats:p>In the K-epsilon framework, a predator-prey like model determines the plasma turbulent transport. It depends on the underlying plasma turbulence via the growth rate chosen for the turbulent energy, the prey K, and its predator epsilon. Compared to our previous work [1], we propose in this paper modifications of the model to be tested in future simulations. A more appropriate expression of the growth rate is proposed by taking into account the fast dynamics of the parallel electron transport. The stabilising terms that are introduced allow for negative values of the growth rate of interchange coupled to drift wave turbulence. Changes to the K-epsilon model are made to adapt it to handle close to marginal states, then allowing one to address a Landau like bifurcation from negative growth rates, without turbulence, to positive growth rates, with turbulence. The closure using the multi-machine SOL width scaling law is revisited to allow the K-epsilon turbulent transport to depend on the growth rate. This is mandatory in the present model to yield increasing turbulent transport towards the edge and enhanced SOL transport governed by the sheath resistivity. Usual predator-prey limit cycles can be achieved whenever the growth rate of the predator is smaller than that of the prey. The growth rates are determined by a simplified 2D turbulence model taking into account magnetic field inhomogeneity and parallel losses, mostly of electrons. These are computed in Fourier space and must be adapted to plasma coarse grained simulations, in particular for edge-SOL-divertor simulations. A growth rate maximisation procedure then determines the wave vector in terms of the plasma parameters. Although the maximisation results are different for drift wave and interchange instabilities, their spectral properties are not discernable and the two instabilities are shown to be difficult to disentangle. Both facets of turbulence are therefore accounted for in the analytical expressions that are obtained for the growth rates, which are to be implemented in K-epsilon simulations of plasma-wall interaction with consistent turbulent transport.</jats:p>

title: A generalized spectral algorithm for fission gas diffusion: Implementation and verification in SCIANTIX
abstract: Fission gas release and swelling in nuclear fuel are governed by the transport of gas atoms from within the grain to the grain boundaries, typically described by diffusion, trapping, and resolution. Under the quasi-stationary approximation, these mechanisms are represented by a diffusion equation with an effective diffusion coefficient, which maintains physical accuracy while reducing computational complexity. While existing spectral solvers typically assume spatially uniform source terms and initial conditions, such simplifications limit the representation of localized phenomena. This work presents a generalized spectral diffusion algorithm implemented in SCIANTIX, an open-source 0D meso -scale code designed to describe fission gas behaviour in nuclear oxide fuel. The algorithm extends the conventional framework of spectral solvers to encompass spatially varying source profiles and non-uniform initial conditions. By accommodating more realistic intra-granular distributions, the solver captures sub-grain-scale effects and enables the exploration of a broader range of physical scenarios such as grain boundary resolution. The implementation is verified using the Method of Manufactured Solutions and demonstrated through case studies. Results show that spatial source heterogeneity influences intragranular retention and gas release kinetics, even with constant volume-averaged gas production. This new framework extends the physical applicability of SCIANTIX to phenomena inherently unrepresentable under uniform-source assumptions.

title: Operational History-Dependent Monte Carlo Multi-Cycle Depletion Analysis of Pakistan Research Reactor-1
abstract: Pakistan Research Reactor-1 (PARR-1) is a Material Testing Reactor (MTR) that has been extensively analyzed using deterministic reactor physics codes. Although some studies have been performed through Monte Carlo models but they were limited by simplifications, such as external multi-group depletion, homogenized structural regions, and uniform axial burnup assumptions. This work addresses these gaps by developing the first high-fidelity, three-dimensional, operational history-dependent Monte Carlo model of PARR-1 using OpenMC code. Three core loadings considered in this work are the first Low-Enriched Uranium (LEU) based high power core, core loadings 93 and 93-A. Simulations were structured to mirror the physical operational procedures. A comprehensive three-way benchmarking was performed, evaluating OpenMC predictions against available measured operational data and WIMS/CITATION deterministic calculations. For Core Loading 93, the OpenMC predictions obtained using the experimental evaluation methodology agree closely with measurements, with differences of +61 pcm, -77 pcm, and -16 pcm for excess reactivity, shutdown margin, and combined control rod reactivity worth, respectively. The calculated thermal neutron flux distribution for Core Loading 93-A reproduces the measured spatial trends, with fuel-element C/E ratios ranging from 0.72 to 1.13. The depletion calculations also reproduce the reported U-235 burnup evolution across successive core loadings. Overall, the developed model preserves fuel-specific irradiation histories and reproduces the neutronic behavior of PARR-1 across multiple operational configurations. This study establishes a validated, continuous-energy Monte Carlo transport-depletion framework for multi-cycle PARR-1 analysis.

title: Fully Integrated Liquid Metal System (FILMS) for a Fusion Reactor: Conceptual Design and Scoping Engineering Analysis
abstract: Fully integrated liquid-metal (LM) plasma-facing and breeding systems offer a promising approach for future fusion reactors capable of simultaneously accommodating high heat loads, tritium breeding, and power conversion. This study introduces and evaluates for the first time the fully integrated liquid metal system (FILMS), a new concept that combines three traditionally separate subsystems into a single liquid-lithium (Li) circuit: (1) a flowing LM first wall, (2) an LM breeding blanket, and (3) an open-surface LM divertor. The Fusion Nuclear Science Facility was used as a representative testbed for integrated thermohydraulic and magnetohydrodynamic (MHD) analyses. Scoping-level analyses were performed to evaluate Li flow rates, temperatures, Reynolds and Hartmann numbers, MHD pressure drops, and pumping-power requirements for the major FILMS circuits. Two structural-material options, reduced activation ferritic martensitic (RAFM) steel and vanadium alloy, were considered together with electrically conducting and electrically insulating wall assumptions. The results demonstrate that electrically insulating configurations, representing flow-channel inserts or electrically insulating sandwich-wall concepts, substantially reduce MHD pressure drops and pumping power. For the electrically insulating vanadium-alloy case, all major circuit pressure drops remain below approximately 2 MPa and the total hydraulic pumping power remains below approximately 1% of the reactor thermal power. In contrast, the electrically insulating RAFM case remains close to the engineering pressure-drop limit and likely requires additional optimization of the inboard blanket and main-loop circuits. The study additionally demonstrates the usefulness of the electric-circuit analogy framework for evaluating coupled flow redistribution and off-design behavior of the integrated FILMS hydraulic network.

title: Design and Implementation of Slow Conventional Controller for the ITER MCTB Quench Protection System
abstract: The magnet cold test bench (MCTB), the key facility of the ITER project, is mainly used for performance verification of superconducting magnets before on-site installation. As an important subsystem of the MCTB, the quench protection system (QPS) utilizes high-power DC switches and commutation technology to achieve rapid current interruption.This paper presents the design and implementation of the slow conventional control system in the QPS, which performs status monitoring and logic control on the key components, including the by-pass switch, vacuum circuit breaker, counter pulse circuit, and pyro-breaker during preparation and test operation. The hardware platform of the QPS takes the Siemens S7-1200 programmable logic controller (PLC) as its core. The software program is developed with TIA Portal, and the supporting human-machine interface (HMI) is programmed via LabVIEW.Real-time full-process data exchange between the PLC and upper HMI is realized through the open platform communications unified architecture protocol. The test results verify that the proposed system integrates the comprehensive status monitoring and logic control functions, runs stably and reliably, and satisfies the engineering application requirements of the QPS.
